items.title: Missing train ticket cannot defeat compensation claim after passenger’s death: Supreme Court
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday held that a missing train ticket could not, by itself, defeat a compensation claim by the parents of a man who died after falling from the train [Sukhabhai Nanjibhai Makwana and Another v. Union of India] A Bench of Justices Ujjal Bhuyan and Atul S Chandurkar set aside a Gujarat High Court ruling that had rejected the parents’ compensation claim after finding insufficient evidence that their son had fallen from a train. “ On preponderance of probabilities, it can be concluded that the victim was a bona fide passenger and that absence of recovery of his ticket cannot result in defeating the claim for compensation, ” the Court said. The Bench thus restored the ₹8 lakh compensation awarded by the Railway Claims Tribunal and directed the Railways to satisfy the award within 30 days. Justices Ujjal Bhuyan and Atul S Chandurkar The case arose from the death of Maheshbhai, who fell from a train between Sabarmati and Ahmedabad railway stations on September 27, 2017. An Additional City Civil and Sessions Judge Shivaprasad KB acquitted Sangamesha, BK Mohan, Ganesh, Basavaraj and Jagadeesh alias Jagannath. Judge Shivaprasad KB Sangamesha and the four other accused had been charged with the offences of criminal conspiracy under Section 120-B of the Indian Penal Code (IPC), rioting under Section 147, attempt to murder under Section 307 read with Section 149 (unlawful assembly), and voluntarily causing grievous hurt under Section 326 read with Section 149 of the IPC. The trial court, however, found glaring defects in the probe. It also observed that at one stage of the investigation, a mentally ill man named Jagadish was made a scapegoat to shield the politically influential accused. In 2018, Jagadish was discharged from the case after the court noted that he was mentally unfit to give evidence. items.title: Husband's girlfriend cannot be booked for cruelty to wife under Section 85 BNS: Karnataka High Court
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court recently quashed criminal proceedings against a woman paramour who was accused of ruining the married relationship of a couple and intimidating the wife. Justice M Nagaprasanna said that the law is settled that a paramour cannot be accused of the offence of cruelty against wife against Section 85 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) since she is not a relative of the husband. In this regard, the Court relied on the Supreme Court's decision in Dechamma IM @ Dechamma Koushik v State of Karnataka in which it was held that a girlfriend of a married man cannot be construed as his relative. "In the light of the bedrock of the law elucidated by the Apex Court, if the facts obtaining in the case at hand are observed, a paramour of the husband - accused No.1 cannot be termed as a relative of the husband," it said. Justice M Nagaprasanna The petitioner (paramour) had approached the High Court after a trial court took cognizance of a criminal case registered against her.
